reader.requirement: At --std 85 a PERFORM that writes procedure-name-1 (any of formats 1 to 4) is out-of-line and executes the named range; one that omits it is in-line and executes its imperative-statement-1 through END-PERFORM; the binder must split on exactly that, and SR1 forbids mixing the two forms.

edition-consulted.switches: refuses an AFTER phrase in an in-line PERFORM before 2002 (§1985:VI.6.21.3 SR2)
UNTIL EXIT is COBOL-2023 only (COBOL0900 at 85)
VARYING with BY omitted refused before 2002
1985 segmentation restriction on the out-of-line range

reader.edition-search: The in-line/out-of-line split itself (names.Length == 0 in BindPerform) consults no edition; the edition gates are on phrases the 1985 formats do not print.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 an in-line PERFORM may not carry AFTER (2002 adds it), and UNTIL EXIT / EXIT PERFORM / BY-omitted are refused; the in-line vs out-of-line classification itself is the same
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb432 and pb440 exercise the VARYING brace and the empty range; mixed-form refusals (SR1) and the 85-only refusals are not exercised there

probes.printed: A..I sections: paragraph, section, THRU paragraph, THRU section, inverted THRU, in-line and out-of-line VARYING (N=004 T=006 both), TEST AFTER (T=006 both), TIMES (3), 0 TIMES, nested in-line, all as expected
probes.expected: out-of-line runs the range, in-line runs its contained statements

probes.printed: error COBOL0306: unexpected 'END-PERFORM' (PERFORM PA DISPLAY "X" END-PERFORM)
error COBOL2269 (in-line PERFORM 2 TIMES with no END-PERFORM)
error COBOL2072 (PERFORM END-PERFORM, no imperative statement)
85: error COBOL0900 an AFTER phrase in an inline PERFORM requires COBOL-2002; 2023: runs 001001..002002 and PA 001001..002002
probes.expected: 85 refuses (§1985:VI.6.21.3 SR2); the out-of-line AFTER is legal

probes.printed: error COBOL0900: PERFORM UNTIL EXIT requires COBOL-2023
error COBOL0900: the EXIT PERFORM statement requires COBOL-2002

reader.notes: GR3 is definitional; BindPerform branches on whether a procedure-name is written, binding BoundInlinePerform or BoundOutOfLinePerform, and the grammar enforces SR1. The 1985-only refusals (in-line AFTER, UNTIL EXIT, EXIT PERFORM, BY omitted) fire at --std 85.
reader.at-2023: p1 prints identical output; c3 runs at 2023

refuter.evidence: Probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-017/r.cbl, run as four variants at --std 85. 'PERFORM PA END-PERFORM', 'PERFORM PA 2 TIMES END-PERFORM', 'PERFORM PA UNTIL T > 1 END-PERFORM' and 'PERFORM PA WITH TEST AFTER UNTIL T > 1 DISPLAY T END-PERFORM' each give error COBOL0306 unexpected END-PERFORM, so SR1 is enforced in every format. E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-017/p2.cbl: an in-line PERFORM holding an IF without END-IF is refused with COBOL2796, which agrees with the 1985 imperative-statement definition (III, a conditional statement counts only when delimited by its scope terminator). The split itself (names.Length==0) consults no edition. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.6.21.4 GR3 ... the text is in GR3'; 'OK  §1985:VI.6.21.3 SR1 ... the text is in SR1'.
